Climate change is reshaping the world we live in, marking the beginning of a new era. As cities, energy, industry, and technology continue to transform, international cooperation has never been more important in shaping our shared future. From November 9 to 20, 2026, Turkey will host COP31, with Antalya as its host city. COP31 will bring together leaders, decision makers, scientists, entrepreneurs, young people, and civil society representatives from around the world, creating a platform for dialogue, consensus, and action on climate change. Spanning more than 1 million square meters, the COP31 site brings this global gathering together across two main hubs: the Blue Zone and the Green Zone. Blue Zone. Covering approximately 527,000 square meters, the Blue Zone is the diplomatic and negotiation center of COP31. From the World Climate Action Summit and official negotiations to country pavilions, presidency events, panels and hundreds of side events, it will host an extensive program at the center of global climate diplomacy. Within approximately 163,000 square meters of built-up space, the site includes a 1,600-seat main plenary hall and a second plenary hall with a capacity of 1,300, alongside 28 meeting rooms, press conference rooms, and spaces for special and side events. 18,850 square meters are allocated to country pavilions, while 6,325 square meters of office space support the working and coordination needs of delegations. Supported by digital infrastructure, meeting facilities, and dedicated workspaces, the Blue Zone brings the key elements of global climate diplomacy together in one center. The Green Zone. While the Blue Zone is where the world negotiates the future, the Green Zone is where climate action, innovation, culture, and public engagement take center stage. Covering approximately 582,000 square meters, the Green Zone connects the climate agenda with society, technology, culture, and everyday life. Zero waste, climate finance, energy and mobility, science and technology, resilient cities, green industrialization, culture and civilization, children and youth, and the startup zone. Together, these themes shape a diverse program of experiences, dialogue, and engagement around climate action and sustainability. At the heart of the Green Zone stands the iconic COP31 tower. At approximately 2,000 square meters, the Turkey Pavilion will serve as a national showcase, presenting Turkey's climate policies, zero-waste vision, energy transition, and sustainable urban development to an international audience. A 5,000-seat main amphitheater and an 800-seat small amphitheater extend this program into the open air. cultural dimension of the Green Zone includes the Anatolian Garden and 7 regions, 7 cuisines, bringing together the cultural and gastronomic heritage of Anatolia with nature, local production, and a zero-waste approach.
